author: The Infographics Show
description:
Your Smart TV may be watching you just as closely as you’re watching it.

Many modern televisions use Automated Content Recognition, or ACR, to identify what appears on the screen. That can include streaming shows, cable, gaming consoles, Blu-rays, and even content coming through HDMI. The data can then be used to build detailed viewing profiles for advertising.
Texas has already sued major manufacturers including Samsung, LG, Sony, Hisense, and TCL over how this technology is disclosed and used. Samsung and LG later agreed to stronger consent and privacy protections in Texas.
The problem goes beyond one brand. Smart TVs have become part hardware product, part advertising platform, and the data generated after you buy the TV can be worth more than the television itself.

Before your next movie night, your privacy settings may be worth checking.

description:
How are Americans buying $500,000 homes on average salaries? In many cases, the answer is builder incentives.

Major homebuilders like D.R. Horton and Lennar now control much more of the buying process, from construction to mortgages, title services, and insurance. To keep homes moving, they can offer huge incentives and temporary mortgage-rate buydowns that make expensive houses look affordable. But those lower payments don’t last forever. Once the subsidy ends, buyers face the full mortgage rate, while property taxes, insurance, and other costs keep rising. Some homeowners are already spending more than half their income on housing, and growing numbers of recent mortgages are underwater.

The house may be affordable today. The real test comes when the teaser rate disappears.
